Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references past NHL expansions (Vegas 2017-18, Seattle 2021-22, Utah 2024-25)
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [NO]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — potential 33rd NHL franchise targeting 2029-30 or 2030-31 season

Synopsis:
    NHL deputy commissioner Bill Daly is tempering expectations around a potential 33rd NHL franchise in Texas (Houston or Austin), backed by Houston billionaire Dan Friedkin at a $2B expansion fee. Daly emphasizes this is a non-binding term sheet — not a done deal on either side — with key hurdles remaining, including arena construction. The league sees strategic value in Texas given Houston's scale (7.8M metro) and Austin's first-mover opportunity among major leagues, but no firm timeline is locked in.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US stocks, US investments?
Relevance: NO — the article is focused on NHL league expansion strategy and sports franchise development, not US macroeconomics, equities, or investment markets broadly.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 20 — the Texas expansion prospect was already publicly floated by Daly last month; this article largely walks back prior optimism, confirming uncertainty rather than introducing a new or unexpected development.
